context: OR 4 is equivalent to the OR which was reported by Curiotto et al. for copper on the same plane of sapphire [39]. Not all the abnormal grains which were investigated had an exact low-index OR with the substrate. Some grains deviated (up to 6° ) from one of the low-index ORs listed above as depicted in Fig. 8. While a low-index OR implies a low-energy OR, at this stage the Pt films are still partly continuous, have not yet reached equilibrium, and the Pt grains are constrained by neighboring grains. In addition, some of the angular deviation from a low-index OR may be due to strain fields resulting from lattice mismatch with the substrate (∼4.3%) and the difference in thermal expansion coefficient between Pt and sapphire, as presented in Fig. 7d. Detailed analysis of the normal-sized grains far from the hole revealed that ∼50% deviate (by up to 6° ) from one of the low-index ORs listed above, where the remainder do not have a low-index OR with the substrate (Fig. 8).
